A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same flow-map self-distillation work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial revision and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original checkerboard and CIFAR-10 experiments, including KL/FID scores, generated samples, and training-gradient measurements in Section 4 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on checkerboard, CIFAR-10, CelebA-64, and AFHQ-64, with quantitative results and generated samples in Section 5 and Appendix G.

M1.justification: The three self-distillation families remain, but v2 adds conditional and classifier-free-guided formulations with conditioning inputs, guidance-scale sampling, and dedicated objectives (Section 3, Appendix F.5). Algorithm 1 also changes the training prescription to separate diagonal and off-diagonal loss batches, with explicit stopgradient variants. The guidance extension is proposed but not evaluated.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from checkerboard and CIFAR-10 to include unconditional face generation on CelebA-64 and animal generation on AFHQ-64 (v2 Table 1 and Appendix G). Both original tasks remain. Conditional generation and guidance are discussed but do not constitute additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain LSD, ESD, PSD-M, and PSD-U on checkerboard, and LSD/PSD comparisons plus unsuccessful ESD training on CIFAR-10. The added image datasets use these same methods. Newly discussed methods such as MeanFlow and Align Your Flow are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: Reported training protocols change substantially: v2 adopts 75% diagonal batches and removes warm-up/annealing. Checkerboard width increases from 256 to 512 and batch size from 64,000 to 100,000. CIFAR-10 changes from 180,000 staged training steps at learning rate 0.001 to 400,000 steps at 0.01, with revised residual blocks and attention. Adam becomes RAdam, and the new image datasets receive separate 800,000-step protocols.

E4.justification: The step-count sweeps and gradient-norm study remain. v2 adds qualitative pilot comparisons of EMA versus instantaneous teachers and embeddings of (s,t-s) versus (s,t), and reports ESD instability across attempted stopgradient configurations (Appendices F.4 and G.2). v1's reported pilot comparison favoring off-diagonal-only sampling disappears. These are limited ancillary checks, not a systematic component-ablation suite.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent training-run counts, aggregated seed results, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both use fixed-noise qualitative comparisons. The additional EMA and evaluation-sample details in v2 do not provide uncertainty estimates across runs.

E6.justification: CIFAR-10 rankings reverse: v1 Table 2 reports one-step FID 38.01 for LSD versus 14.13 for PSD-U; v2 Table 1 reports 8.10 versus 13.61, with LSD leading at every reported step count. Checkerboard changes from PSD-U leading for two or more steps to LSD leading through eight steps. CelebA-64 and AFHQ-64 results are added. These are revised/new results under changed settings, not controlled performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: v2 adds continuity to Proposition 2.2, supplies characterization proofs and a discontinuous counterexample explaining the assumption, and develops continuous-time derivations connecting consistency training, MeanFlow, and Align Your Flow (Appendices C-E). It also corrects the ESD time index in equation (14) and restores the missing (t-s)^2 factor in the PSD loss identity. The principal Wasserstein bounds are retained.

C1.justification: The general self-distillation contribution remains, but the headline empirical claim changes. v1 emphasizes avoiding temporal and spatial derivatives for image synthesis, favoring PSD. v2 instead presents Lagrangian methods as more stable and better performing than Eulerian and Progressive methods, and explicitly claims that the framework encompasses all known consistency-model distillation and direct-training schemes.

C2.justification: v2 shifts the explanation toward spatial Jacobians, stopgradient placement, and LSD's avoidance of bootstrapping. It newly attributes PSD's theoretical difficulty to compounding errors and distribution shift (Section 2.3), discusses uncertain convergence of stopgradient updates, and expands limitations concerning untested parameterizations, stabilization choices, hybrid objectives, and guidance. These materially revise the interpretation and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code link, method-specific pseudocode, a configuration table, explicit histogram-based KL computation, FID checkpoint-selection procedures, EMA values, clipping, and embedding details. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing that every newly disclosed procedure changed. Some information is lost or inconsistent: v1's CIFAR GPU disclosure disappears, and v2 Table 2 lists 10,000 AFHQ evaluation samples while Appendix G.4 specifies 50,000.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands research positioning through dedicated derivations relating the framework to consistency training/distillation, MeanFlow, Align Your Flow, and shortcut models (Appendices B-D). It adds corresponding citations and emphasizes the distinctness of Lagrangian formulations. The operator-learning connection and Zheng et al. reference present in v1 are removed; the changes extend beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and algorithm discussion are extensively rewritten. Related work moves from Section 1.1 to Section 4, a conclusion is added, and the appendices are reorganized into dedicated connections, proofs, algorithmic details, and experimental subsections. Existing material is substantially restructured alongside the scientific additions.

P2.justification: The two original results tables become an expanded combined Table 1, and a new configuration Table 2 is added. Figure 5 expands into a three-dataset sample grid; checkerboard plots are regenerated, with Figure 3 changing its displayed multistep row from 16 to eight steps. Three detailed algorithm displays are added, while the principal schematics are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens theoretical completeness by stating the continuity needed for the flow-map characterization, explaining its necessity, and supplying fuller proofs and connections. Detailed algorithms and metric/checkpoint procedures address important reproducibility omissions in v1, while two additional image domains broaden validation. Changed training settings prevent isolating the cause of the reversed rankings, and the AFHQ sample-count conflict remains. These limitations temper the empirical conclusions but do not outweigh the substantial gains in theoretical support and reproducibility.
